object_description: long three-story building with notched upper floors and gabled ends
design_condition: The building follows the neighbouring buildings’ orientation and scale, minimally alters the terrain, and creates a school square toward the landscape and village alongside a garden square by the retirement home.

positive.statement: The chosen position is fundamentally plausible and does not disturb the striking lime tree hill.

position.rationale: The hill is absent from the sampled exterior; a low south-west site anchor approximates its landscape relationship.

positive.statement: The entrances are convincing, with covered vestibules differentiated according to their importance.

position.rationale: The south-facing edge provides the most plausible sampled surface for differentiated principal access points.

positive.statement: The staggered room groups create a learning landscape that almost ideally implements the desired pedagogical concept.

position.rationale: Top view visibly shows repeated staggered groups and notches through the building’s central length.

positive.statement: The planned lighting creates landmarks that support clear navigation through the diverse spatial structure.

position.rationale: Lighting devices are not identifiable, so the upper central mass supplies a constrained landmark anchor.

positive.statement: The building envelope coherently reflects the construction method and internal organization.

position.rationale: Elongated envelope, notches, and gabled ends are legible across top and elevation views.

positive.statement: The compact building is likely to be economical to build and operate and meets contemporary ecological objectives.

position.rationale: Economy, operation, and ecological performance are global judgments without a single spatial referent.

positive.statement: The clear structures and rich composition create a unique spatial experience contributing to an unmistakable identity.

position.rationale: The sampled building expresses identity through elongated massing and varied notched composition.

negative.statement: It is not initially apparent why the new building is not positioned at right angles to the sports facilities and surrounding buildings.

position.target: building orientation to sports facilities and surrounding buildings
position.rationale: The model establishes a strong east-west axis, while neighboring facilities are absent; the south site edge anchors it.

negative.statement: The organization of the meeting rooms does not always meet users’ needs, although simple internal optimization appears possible.

position.rationale: Meeting rooms are not distinguishable; the eastern central room-group area provides a plausible estimate.

negative.statement: The music room’s location between two school rooms is assessed critically.

position.target: music room between two school rooms
position.rationale: The specific music room is absent, so the central staggered room band constrains its approximate location.
